ModMetaData.name: Automated Work Assignment
ModMetaData.author: Ekinox0310
ModMetaData.description:
Tired of juggling work priorities every time your colony grows? Automated Work Assignment fills in the Work tab for you, putting each colonist on the jobs they are best at and most passionate about.
Spend less time micromanaging the priority grid and more time running your colony.
=== How it works ===
For every work type you decide how many colonists should do it (a fixed number or a percentage of the colony) and at which priority (1 = most urgent, 4 = least). The mod scores every colonist by Skill Level plus a Passion bonus, gives the job to the best candidates, and handles everyone else with a backup priority of your choice (or turns the job off for them).
Assignments refresh automatically once per day, or instantly with the Refresh button on the Work tab.
=== Features ===
Three assignment modes: - Simple Mode: count/percentage, priority, passion weight and backup priority per job. - Expert Mode: skill-range rules per job (e.g. "skill 0-5 = P4, skill 12-20 = P1"), with optional "passion first" sorting to train passionate colonists. - Hybrid Mode: Expert rules apply where they match; Simple Mode settings cover everything else.
Smart priorities: - Emergency priorities: optionally force Doctor and Firefighter to priority 1 for assigned colonists. - Passion weight from 0x (ignore passion) to 3x (strongly prefer passionate pawns), per job or with one global slider. - Gradual priority bands: instead of giving every backup colonist the same number, spread them across a priority range by skill. The same can be applied to the main group, optionally keeping one "lead" pawn at the top (one head doctor or head cook plus helpers). - Percentages can round up to the next whole colonist (25% of 5 colonists = 2 instead of 1).
Control and exclusions: - Exclude colonists from automation entirely, or only from specific jobs. - Optionally leave children out of automation. - Turn off automation for individual work types. - Combine related work types (e.g. Growing + Cut plants) into one settings row.
Convenient UI: - Buttons on the Work tab: turn the mod ON/OFF, Refresh Now, and open the settings. - Standalone settings window: draggable, resizable, with collapsible sections and explanations for every option. - Settings are saved per save game.
Experimental (WIP): a player-profiling module that only collects local context data when enabled. It does not change assignments yet and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
=== Compatibility ===
- Works with work types added by other mods; they show up in the settings automatically. - Supports Vanilla Skills Expanded passions. - RimWorld 1.5, 1.6 and 1.7. - Requires Harmony.
Languages: English, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French.
=== FAQ ===
Q: Is it compatible with "Work Tab" by Fluffy? A: Probably not. Both mods change the Work tab and the priority system, so one may overwrite the other. Use only one mod to manage work priorities.
Q: Is it compatible with AI/scheduling mods (Achtung!, Pawn Rules, etc.)? A: Generally yes. This mod only sets the priority numbers; other mods read them to decide what to do. Major conflicts are unlikely, but testing is always recommended.
Q: Does it affect performance? A: Very little. The full assignment runs once per in-game day or when you press Refresh. It does not react to every skill change.
Q: How does it decide who is best? A: In Simple Mode, a score based on the colonist's relevant skill plus a passion bonus scaled by the passion weight. In Expert Mode, by the skill-range rules you define.
Q: Can I still set priorities by hand? A: Yes. Turn the mod off, exclude a colonist (globally or for one job), or turn off automation for a work type, and the mod will leave those priorities alone.
Q: Does it respect zones, schedules, outfits, etc.? A: Yes. The mod only sets priority numbers (1-4 or off). Allowed areas, work times, apparel, tools and every other base game rule still apply.
Q: A colonist has priority 1 for a job but isn't doing it. Why? A: Check the usual RimWorld reasons: another priority-1 job ranked earlier, zone restrictions, schedule (sleep/recreation), injuries or bed rest, missing materials, or no path to the work.
Q: Does it manage Patient / Bed Rest? A: No. The game handles those automatically. The mod helps by keeping assigned doctors at priority 1 when emergency priorities are on.
Q: Can I add it to an existing save? A: Yes. Configure the settings, then press Refresh Now or wait for the daily refresh.
Please report any bugs you find.
